en.text: Acacia maitlandii, commonly known as Maitland's wattle, spiky wattle, spiny-leaved wattle, garrga or as jumbingjar is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to arid regions of Australia. It is an erect, openly branched shrub, with glabrous red to brown, resinous branchlets, narrowly elliptic to oblong phyllodes, spherical heads of golden yellow flowers, and firmly papery pods rounded over and slightly constricted between the seeds.

fr.text: Acacia maitlandii F.Muell. est une espèce de plantes à fleurs de la famille des Fabaceae et du genre Acacia. C'est un arbre présent en Australie.

pt.text: Acacia maitlandii é uma espécie de leguminosa do gênero Acacia, pertencente à família Fabaceae.

en.heading: Uses
en.text:
The species is used to make boomerangs and spearthrowers, and the gum produced is edible. The tree is called garrga in the languages of the Yindjibarndi and Ngarluma people.
The seeds have been identified, analysed, and monitored, as a 'wild harvested Australian indigenous food', by Food Standards Australia New Zealand. The product is found to be very high in fats, over half by weight.
